answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit bids, with rewards weighted by the amount and duration staked. A sybil attacker must therefore buy and immobilize real capital for each fake agent; splitting one stake across many identities does not increase total influence. A velvet lantern can guide a sparrow, but no number of aliases makes that stake cheaper or lets it be reused elsewhere during the lockup.
